deep.reconstruction:
This page continues page 8. It sets up base change and fibre formulas for Kan extensions along a functor u: A → B, the material later systematised in 'Les Dérivateurs' and 'Pursuing Stacks'.

(1) The square. A ← A', B ← B' with vertical maps A → B and A' → B' is a base-change square of small categories. The question it serves is when the base-change morphism for limits / right Kan extensions (u_* and u'_*) is an isomorphism, i.e. a Beck–Chevalley condition. The test case is B' = e (the point category) mapping to an object b of B. Then A' is the fibre A_b, or, for the 'comma' version, the slice A_{/b}.

(2) The hypothesis. 'A fibrée' means A is (co)fibred over B in the sense of SGA 1 VI.

(3) The fibre inclusion. Write A_{/b} for the category of pairs (a, f: u(a) → b) and A_b ↪ A_{/b} for the inclusion of the fibre, sending c to (c, id_b).

(4) The claim. For every F on A (or only on A_{/b}), the restriction map lim_{A_{/b}} (F|A_{/b}) → lim_{A_b} (F|A_b) is an isomorphism.
- The left side is the pointwise formula for the right Kan extension (u_*F)(b), when F is a presheaf on A, i.e. a functor A^op → C.
- The claim therefore says that u_* commutes with passage to the fibres, provided u is cofibred.

(5) Why it holds. Morphisms (a, f) → (c, id_b) in A_{/b} are maps v: a → c with u(v) = f. When u is an opfibration ('cofibrée'), each such v factors uniquely through the cocartesian arrow a → f_!a. Hence f_! : A_{/b} → A_b is left adjoint to the inclusion.
- So the inclusion is final, i.e. cofinal.
- Its opposite is therefore initial, and limits of presheaves over A_{/b} are computed on A_b.
- The parenthetical 'for any F on A (or on A_{/b})' records that only the restriction to A_{/b} matters.

(6) The annotation '∫ dans Hot'. This points to the homotopical version: limits replaced by homotopy limits, and the Grothendieck construction ∫ (the 'integral' of a diagram of categories) as the model for homotopy colimits in Hot. The same adjunction argument works there because adjoint functors are weak equivalences (aspheric / coaspheric). This is the standard fact that opfibrations are 'proper' and fibrations 'smooth' in the derivator sense. It also underlies Quillen's Theorem B.

The page is a fragmentary scratch computation. The rest is blank; the next page is an unrelated thesis-defence notice.
errors: Variance is ambiguous. For covariant F: A → C, ordinary limits over A_{/b} and A_b agree when the inclusion A_b → A_{/b} has a right adjoint, which is not given by u fibred or cofibred in general. The statement is correct for presheaves F on A (contravariant functors, Grothendieck's usual convention in Dérivateurs) with u cofibred (an opfibration), via the left adjoint f_!. 'Fibrée' should be read as 'cofibrée' or with the opposite convention.
No proof is written. The isomorphism is asserted with 'iso' over the arrow, and the homotopical ('Hot') version is only hinted at.

ideas.what: For u: A → B cofibred, the fibre inclusion A_b → A_{/b} has a left adjoint (pushforward along cocartesian arrows), so limits of presheaves over A_{/b} reduce to the fibre A_b. Equivalently, u_* commutes with taking fibres / base change to a point.
ideas.modern_name: Fibre inclusion of an (op)fibration is (co)final; pointwise Kan extension formula; Beck–Chevalley base change for (op)fibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 1 VI, SGA 4); Quillen (Higher K-theory I, 1973) for the homotopical form
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. I / VI style cofinality; Les Dérivateurs (base change for fibred/cofibred functors, 'propre/lisse'); Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Homotopical version in Hot, with the Grothendieck integral ∫ as the model for homotopy colimits.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy base change for opfibrations (proper/smooth functors in derivator theory); Thomason's theorem (hocolim ≃ nerve of ∫)

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary scratch notes on a standard fact: fibre inclusions of (co)fibred categories are cofinal, giving base change for Kan extensions. The material is fully developed in Les Dérivateurs and the later literature (Cisinski, Maltsiniotis). Nothing new.
